records.name: Philadelphia Classical Guitar Society
records.summary: A nonprofit that presents classical guitar concerts, a festival, and a competition in Philadelphia and Newtown, PA. It also runs a guitar ensemble and hosts guitar salons.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets for the concert season, or drop in on a free Sunday guitar salon, where members play short pieces for listeners. Intermediate and advanced players of any age can apply to the Concert Ensemble, a guitar orchestra for PCGS members, after an audition.

schedule.text: Guitar salons are held on Sundays during the concert season, starting at 1:30 pm. Concerts run on weekends from November to March. The Concert Ensemble rehearses on Sundays from 11 am to 1 pm, usually twice a month.

locations.label: Guitar salons and most Concert Ensemble rehearsals (Settlement Music School)

cost.text: Guitar salons are free, and listeners are welcome. Concert tickets are sold separately, and prices are not on the home page. The Concert Ensemble fee is $300 per player for the season, and PCGS Professional members are exempt.

first_step.how: Come to a free guitar salon on a Sunday afternoon (it starts at 1:30 pm at Settlement Music School, 416 Queen St), or buy a ticket to a Sunday concert.
first_step.basis: Salons are free, listeners are welcome, and the page says some players are performing for the first time. Players sign up with a short form at least 24 hours ahead, which is a clear way in. The Concert Ensemble is for intermediate and advanced players only.
first_step.what_to_expect: A salon is an informal Sunday afternoon session where members play short pieces, up to 10 minutes each, for a listening audience. Some players are trying a piece out for the first time, and some come to get feedback. The salon is free and in person, and the concert that follows at 3 pm needs a ticket.
first_visit_tips: The salon is free, but the concert after it needs a separate ticket.
If you want to play, fill out the performer form at least 24 hours before the salon, or announce your piece on the day.
Questions about salons go to the board members who run them, whose contact details are on the salon page.

records.notes: The membership page loads without tier or price detail, so no dues are recorded. Players under 18 can join the Concert Ensemble with a signed parental consent form, which is why kids_ok is true; the pages say nothing about age rules for salons or concerts. The ensemble page gives Settlement Music School as both ZIP 19147 and 19118; 19147 is used because the salon page gives it. One salon date on the page has a typo year and is not used. The closest interest tag for the orchestra is community_band. Ensemble audition steps are not published.

records.name: Philadelphia County 4-H (Penn State Extension)
records.summary: Penn State Extension's county 4-H program for young people ages 5 to 18. Its project clubs cover areas such as animal science, civic leadership, the arts, environmental science, health, and STEM.
records.what_you_do: Pick a project club that fits your interests, enroll through the county educator, and take part in that club's projects and events with other youth. Ages 5 to 7 join as Cloverbuds, which does non-competitive activities.

schedule.text: Each project club sets its own meeting times with its county educator, and the club's meeting times are not published. The county office is staffed on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm, with a closure from 1 to 2 pm, so call ahead.

locations.label: County office (mailing address; staff work remotely)

cost.text: Members pay a fee for educational materials. Project fees vary by county and project, and the amounts are not published on the county pages. Financial help is available, so ask the club leader or the county educator.

first_step.how: Choose a project club from the county's club list, then contact the county 4-H educator at PhiladelphiaExt@psu.edu or 215-471-2200 to enroll. Enrollment is done online through the state 4-H enrollment system, or with the educator's help.
first_step.basis: Open to all youth ages 5 to 18, with a clear enrollment path through the county educator. Enrollment and material fees come before the first meeting, and the pages do not describe a first meeting.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pages do not describe a first meeting. The first step is a conversation with the county educator, who helps you choose a club and complete enrollment. Clubs are project based: Cloverbud activities for ages 5 to 7 are non-competitive, and members ages 8 to 18 can take part in competitive events.
first_visit_tips: Call the county office before you go, since it is staffed remotely and closes from 1 to 2 pm.
Ask the educator about a club's meeting times and fees before you enroll.
If the fee is a barrier, ask about the financial help the program offers.
If your project is not offered, a new club needs at least five youth from two families and an adult leader, so ask the educator.

records.notes: The file held for this id described a one-time food forest work day (named Hort Center Food Forest Work Day, listed on the Philadelphia Orchards Project events page). That is an event, not this program, so the name, summary, categories, schedule, location, and the old 2026-10 sign of life were replaced. The work day is in leads_only. The county events page is titled Upcoming Events and lists none. Status is probably_active because the county's own pages show no dated items. The age rules come from the join page: Cloverbuds for ages 5 to 7, the full program for ages 8 to 18.

records.name: Philadelphia Dance Company (PHILADANCO!)
records.summary: A professional dance company that performs in Philadelphia, run alongside a dance school for children and adults. The school teaches ballet, modern, jazz, tap and hip hop.
records.what_you_do: Take a class at The Philadelphia School of Dance Arts, which teaches students from age 4 and adults, or come to a company show. Dancers ages 15 to 23 can be chosen for the apprentice company after an evaluation.

schedule.text: Studio hours at the West Philadelphia studios are Monday to Friday 4 to 9 pm and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm. The West Oak Lane studio is open Monday to Friday 5 to 9 pm and Saturday 10 am to 2 pm. Class times are not on the site, so call to ask.

locations.label: West Philadelphia studios (Philadelphia School of Dance Arts)
West Oak Lane studio (Philadelphia School of Dance Arts)

cost.text: Tuition is not listed on the site, so call the studio for prices. The school's pre-professional training program runs during the school year and is free for participants, with dancewear and counseling included.

first_step.how: Call (215) 387-8202 to ask about open class spots and times, then sign up for a class at the studio you choose.
first_step.basis: The school lists classes from beginner level up, including adult classes, and tells people to call about openings. It does not describe a trial class or a drop-in day.
first_step.what_to_expect: Young children start with pre-dance and acrobat classes, and students from age 7 take classical ballet, modern jazz, and tap. Classical ballet runs from beginner to advanced levels, and adults can take ballet, modern, tap, jazz, or hip hop. Pointe is offered from age 10, once a dancer is physically ready. Call first to confirm open spots, class times, and tuition before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 387-8202 first to confirm open spots and class times, since the site does not post them.
Ask which studio has your class, because the two studios have different hours.
The Oak Lane studio lists a different phone number on the school page, so check it before you call.
Ask about tuition before you sign up, because prices are not posted.

records.notes: Danco on Danco is listed on the events page for October 10 and 11, 2026, at the company's studios on N Preston Street, so the date moved out of what_you_do and into last_sign_of_life. The school page gives Oak Lane hours that differ from the West Philadelphia hours; both are recorded. The dance education page gives two different dates for the junior ensemble (2022 and 2016) and two program lengths (40 and 46 weeks), so neither is recorded. The summer training program admits students by audition each June. Adult class levels are not listed. The entry rules for the free training program are not stated.

records.name: Philadelphia Dance Theatre
records.summary: A classical ballet school and performing company in Mount Airy, founded in 1998. Its training runs from preschool through adult classes, and its company dances an annual Nutcracker and a spring new-works show.
records.what_you_do: Take the free trial class, then enroll in ballet classes for ages 3 and up. Boys who take ballet can join the tuition-free boys' program, or come to the company's Nutcracker and spring shows.

schedule.text: Ballet classes run through the school year in four divisions: preschool (ages 3 to 6), primary (ages 7 to 12), pre-professional (ages 13 to 18), and adult (18 and up). Class times are posted as an image on the class schedule page, so call the studio to read them. The company performs A Philadelphia Nutcracker each December and a spring new-works show.

cost.text: The first class is free. Monthly tuition runs from $95 for pre-ballet to $475 for the top levels, billed over nine months from September to May, plus a $50 registration fee per student each year. Siblings get 15 percent off family tuition. Boys in the tuition-free program pay no tuition when they meet its weekly class minimums, but they still pay the $50 registration fee.

first_step.how: Fill out the trial class form on the website to get a class recommendation, take the free trial class, then get placed in a level and register through the studio's Dance StudioPro portal.
first_step.basis: The studio has a set path for newcomers: a free first class, a recommendation form, and faculty placement. Classes are open to the public, and the site explains each step.
first_step.what_to_expect: The free trial class lets a dancer try the studio while faculty choose the right level and classes. Afterward, faculty suggest a schedule, and you register online through the studio's portal. Classes are grouped into preschool, primary, pre-professional, and adult divisions.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the trial class form before you come, since it starts the class recommendation.
Check the dress code page before the trial class, and contact the office about anything the site does not cover.
Parking and transit are not listed on the site, so ask the office before your first visit.

records.notes: The class schedule is an image, so class days and times could not be read and are left out. The tuition page gives no school year for its monthly amounts. The homepage dates (fall classes, auditions) carry no year; the 2026 fall start date comes from the class schedule page. The boys' program lists no age range or audition. The founding year in the summary is carried from tier 1 and was not re-checked.

records.name: Philadelphia Ethical Society
records.summary: A humanist community at Rittenhouse Square that holds free Sunday talks with a guest speaker and live music. The talks are open in person and online, with dialogue on making Philadelphia more ethical.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free Sunday talk at 11 am, in person at Rittenhouse Square or online. To become a member, attend events for a while, fill out the interest form, and talk with members and the board about applying.

schedule.text: Sunday talks at 11 am each week, with a guest speaker, live music, and dialogue. The calendar also lists other events, such as yoga, dance classes, and a film club.

cost.text: Admission to Sunday talks costs nothing, and the public is welcome. Giving to support the society is optional, with monthly tiers starting at $10.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday talk at 1906 Rittenhouse Square at 11 am, or watch live online. To get the online link, sign up for the mailing list.
first_step.basis: Talks are free and open to the public, both in person and online, with a clear way to get the online link. The site has no first-visit guide or newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Sunday program at 11 am features a guest speaker and live music, plus a conversation about making Philadelphia more ethical. Talks are livestreamed and recorded, and past sessions are on the society's YouTube channel. The site does not say how long the program runs.
first_visit_tips: The site gives no entrance or elevator details, so call the office at 215-735-3456 before a first visit.
Sign up for the mailing list if you want the link to watch online.
Check the event page for an RSVP link, since the site does not say whether one is required.
Watch a past session on the YouTube channel to get a sense of the program first.

records.notes: The tier 1 summary said a discussion follows each talk. The pages read in this pass describe a dialogue as part of the Sunday program but do not say it comes after the talk, so the summary now says dialogue is part of the talk. The pricing page says a monthly Introduction to Ethical Culture discussion appears on the calendar, but the calendar page did not show it, so it is not recorded. The membership path has no dues listed; the page lists monthly giving tiers. The homepage dates with years are Aug 17, Oct 8, Oct 10 and Oct 14, 2026. Entrance, elevator, parking and transit are not stated.

records.name: Philadelphia Falcons Soccer Club
records.summary: A soccer club in Philadelphia whose members are mostly LGBTQIA+ players. It runs weekly indoor and outdoor pickup games, leagues and tournaments, and welcomes anyone who wants to play.
records.what_you_do: Play a weekly pickup game, which non-members can try once, then join the club to keep playing. The club also runs leagues and tournaments.

schedule.text: Weekly outdoor pickup games are on Mondays from 6:30 to 8:30 pm at Chew Playground. Indoor futsal pickup runs too, but the site gives no schedule for it. The club posts seasonal changes on its pickup page.

cost.text: Pickup is free, and non-members can join one. Membership is needed to keep playing, and its fee is not listed on the pages checked. A scholarship application is offered.

requirements.gear: A light shirt and a dark shirt, plus water. Cleats are recommended for outdoor play, and indoor shoes are required for indoor futsal.

first_step.how: Come to a Monday pickup at Chew Playground (6:30 to 8:30 pm) as a guest, sign the non-member waiver, then register for a membership on the club's LeagueApps site to keep playing.
first_step.basis: The pickup page says all skill levels are welcome, non-members can try one session, and it explains how to register after that.
first_step.what_to_expect: Pickup is an outdoor game on a grass field, and all skill levels are welcome. Bring a light shirt and a dark shirt plus water, and wear cleats outdoors. The page does not say how many players attend or how teams are formed.
first_visit_tips: Bring a light shirt and a dark shirt, plus water.
Wear cleats for the outdoor game, and indoor shoes if you come to futsal.
Non-members sign a waiver, which is linked from the Play menu on the club's site.
Email sportingactivities@phillyfalcons.org with questions before you come.

records.notes: Status is active on a schedule notice dated August 2026 (a late summer pickup schedule), not on an event post. The club calendar lists no events and points to a Google Calendar subscription. Membership fees, league dates and tournament dates are not published on the pages checked. The club's own domain redirects to its LeagueApps site, and the redirect was followed. The Monday pickup time and place come from the late summer schedule and may change. Kids_ok is carried from tier 1.

records.name: Philadelphia Folksong Society
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs the Philadelphia Folk Festival each August, a Folk School in Roxborough, and concert series. The festival includes song circles, jam sessions, and open mic time.
records.what_you_do: Buy a day pass or camping ticket for the festival, go to a concert, or volunteer for a festival committee. A volunteer ticket also counts as your registration.

schedule.text: The Philadelphia Folk Festival runs one weekend each August, Friday through Sunday, at Old Pool Farm. Concerts and the Folk School keep their own calendars.

locations.label: Festival site at Old Pool Farm, Upper Salford Township
Folk School and offices in Roxborough

cost.text: Festival tickets cost money, with day passes, camping packages, and a VIP package. Society members get discounted festival tickets. Children under 5 enter free with an adult.

first_step.how: Buy a day pass or concert ticket on the festival's tickets page, or sign up to volunteer through the volunteers page.
first_step.basis: The festival and concerts are open to anyone with a ticket, and volunteer committees name jobs for first-timers. The pages checked describe no beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival is an outdoor, multi-day event with music on seven stages from 11 am into the evening, plus camping, crafts, food, and family activities. You can attend for a single day. Camping has its own arrival days and a wristband to enter, and a golf-cart shuttle runs on the grounds.
first_visit_tips: Read the parking and camping pages before you go, since the site is temporary and the ground is rough.
Pets are not allowed, except licensed or registered service dogs.
The FAQ says amplified instruments and drumming are not allowed.
Camping ticket holders get staggered entry days, so check your ticket before you travel.

access.notes: ADA camping sites and ADA parking are inside the camping gate. A golf-cart shuttle (TramCart) runs on the concert and camping grounds. The ground is rough because the site is temporary.

records.notes: Folk School: no class list or current schedule was found on the group's pages or in one web search. The Roxborough location is carried from tier 1 and a 2018 move report, and no street address was verified, so none is recorded. Song circles, jam sessions and open mic (in the summary) were not found on the festival pages read; they are kept from tier 1 but are unconfirmed. Under-5 free entry in cost is carried from tier 1 and is not on the FAQ. Volunteer ticket prices are not recorded because the volunteer page does not state the year. Ticket prices are on the tickets page, which was not read in this pass. The 2026 festival dates (August 14 to 16) appear on the homepage with the year written.
